title: The Ayodhya dispute: A detailed timeline from 1528 to 2020
description: Prime Minister Narendra Modi is all set to lay the foundation stone of the Ram Temple in Ayodhya on 5th August, 2020. Preparations are underway in full swing in the temple town for the grand 'bhoomi poojan'. The ceremony on August 5 will be the culmination of a legal tussle that lasted for many decades and saw several twists and turns along the way. From the setting up of the Babri mosque in Ayodhya in 1528 to its demolition and the legal battle over ownership of the land, the dispute created a huge divide in the Indian society and also led to several incidents of communal violence in the country. The final verdict in the case came on November 19, 2019, when a five-judge Constitution bench of the Supreme Court headed by then CJI Ranjan Gogoi allotted the disputed land to the Ramjanmabhoomi Trust and ordered the government to provide an alternative piece of five acres of land to the Muslim side for a mosque. Watch this video for a complete timeline of the Ayodhya dispute from 1528 to its eventual resolution in 2019.

asr.full_text: After a legal tussle spreading over several decades, the foundation of the Ram temple is set to be laid on 5th of August 2020. Here's a brief timeline of how the dispute started, the various twists and turns, and its culmination in the 2019 judgement by the Supreme Court. The dispute began back in 1528, when Babur's Commander Mir Baki built the Babri Mosque. At the core of the dispute is the belief that Lord Ram was born in a room located under the central dome of the mosque. The British in 1859 erected a fence to divide the area of worship allowing the inner court to be used by Muslims and the outer court by Hindus. In 1885 Mahant Raghuvir Das filed a plea in the Faizabad district court seeking permission to build a temple outside the Babri Mosque structure in the Ram Chhabutra. The plea was however rejected. In 1949, Idol of Ramlalla mysteriously appeared inside the Babri Mosque. Muslims allege the idol was kept inside by Hindus leading to protests followed by Civil Suits from both sides. The premise was then declared a disputed area and locked up in 1950 a plea was filed in Faizabad Court seeking permission to worship the Ramlalai idol in 1959 nirmai Akhadha entered the fray and filed a civil suit seeking possession of the disputed land two years later the UP central Sunni Waqf Board filed a plea for possession of the Babri Masjid. They also sought removal of Lord Ram's idol from the mosque. In 1983 the Vishwa Hind Parishad started a nationwide movement for the construction of the temple. In 1986 on a plea filed by Harishankar Dube, a district judge directed the masjid gates be unlocked to allow Hindus to pray. All cases related to the title suit were transferred to the Allahabad High Court in 1989. In the same year, VHP carried out Shalanya's ceremony in Ayodhya, and the first stone of the planned Ram temple was put in place. In September then BJP President L. K. Advani led a Radh Yatra to Ayodhya demanding the construction of a temple. This led to communal violence and clashes in many parts. In 1991 BJP won the polls in Uttar Pradesh and came to power in the state. The Kalyan Singh government then acquired 2.77 acre of land around the disputed site. ln Dec. 1992, Karsevaks demolished the Babri Masjid. This was followed by communal riots. In 1993, the President issued orders for acquisition of certain areas around the disputed site. The matter was also referred to the Supreme Court for its opinion, in 1994 in the Kamal Faruqi case. The Supreme Court said, that a mosque was not integral to Islam. In 2002 the Allahabad High Court began hearing to determine ownership of the land. Seventeen years after the demolition, the Liber Khan Commission, appointed to probe the incident, submitted its report in 2009. It named several prominent BJP leaders, including Vajpayee and Advani. In 2010, the Allahabad High Court ordered a three-way division of the disputed area between the Sunni Waqf board, Nirmohi Akhada and Ramlala. In 2011, The Supreme Court stayed the High Court Verdict after petitions were filed challenging it in the Top Court. In March 2019, The Top Court appointed a Mediation Panel with FM KalifulA and Sm Mravi Shankar and senior advocate SSR Ram Panchu as members. But, the mediation panel failed to solve the dispute. The Supreme Court gave its verdict on 9th November 2019. The Order paved the way for a temple at the disputed site and ordered the Government to allot five acres of land to Muslims in another location.
